## Motivation

This analysis explores per-class reservation windows for weighted patient classes under oversubscribed FCFS scheduling. The primary interest is the interaction between reservation window length and delay-dependent balking: when does a wider window help a class, and when does balking erode the benefit?

## Objective Function

The primary objective is the additive weighted served rate:

$$U(w_1, w_2) = w_1 \frac{Y_1}{A_1} + w_2 \frac{Y_2}{A_2}$$

where $Y_i$ is served patients and $A_i$ is arrivals for class $i$. When $w_1 = w_2 = 1$, this reduces to the sum of per-class served rates. When $w_1 > 1$, the objective values Class 1 access more heavily.

Two diagnostics are reported alongside the objective: no-offer rate per class ($N_i / A_i$), which captures the direct access effect of the window, and mean offered delay per class, which captures the delay composition of offers received.

A secondary objective — the pooled weighted served rate $(w_1 Y_1 + w_2 Y_2) / (w_1 A_1 + w_2 A_2)$ — is compared against the primary in the divergence section.

## Experimental Design

Each simulation run assigns per-class booking horizons ($H_1$, $H_2$), per-class balking thresholds ($\tau_1$, $\tau_2$), and a shared post-threshold balking rate ($b_1$). All other parameters are held at baseline. Each configuration is replicated across 50 seeds.

| Parameter | Values |
|-----------|--------|
| Horizons ($H_1$, $H_2$) | 2, 5, 7, 10, 14 — all 25 pairs |
| Balking thresholds ($\tau_1$, $\tau_2$) | (9,9), (5,9), (9,5), (12,12), (5,12) |
| Post-threshold balking rate ($b_1$) | 0.3, 0.5, 0.7 |
| Weight regimes | $w_1 = 1.0$ (equal), $w_1 = 2.0$ (priority) |
| Total configurations | 375 × 50 seeds = 18,750 runs |

## No-Offer Rate and Offered Delay Diagnostics

The no-offer rate is the primary channel through which the window acts. Shorter windows produce lower mean offered delays, but this reflects a change in sample composition: patients who would have received long-delay offers instead receive no offer at all.

![No-offer rate by class](../../../outputs/reservation_window/figures/fig3_no_offer_rate.png)

![Offered delay by class](../../../outputs/reservation_window/figures/fig4_offered_delay.png)

## Objective Function Divergence

The secondary objective — the pooled weighted served rate — computes a single weighted ratio rather than summing per-class rates:

$$U_{pooled}(w_1, w_2) = \frac{w_1 Y_1 + w_2 Y_2}{w_1 A_1 + w_2 A_2}$$
